ShortDef: A packaged app plus everything it needs, run in isolation from other apps on the same machine.
Details: Containers share the host's kernel, so they start in seconds and use far less than virtual machines. An image is the read-only template; a container is a running instance of it.
WhenToUse: Making 'it works on my machine' true everywhere, and packing many services on one host.

ShortDef: The built, layered, read-only package a container starts from; a Dockerfile is the recipe.
Details: Each instruction in a Dockerfile adds a cached layer. Order them so rarely-changing steps come first. Multi-stage builds keep build tools out of the final image.
WhenToUse: Whenever you build or ship software in containers.

ShortDef: A server that stores and serves container images (Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR, ACR).
Details: CI builds an image, tags it with a version, and pushes it; clusters pull it. Scan images in the registry for known vulnerabilities.
WhenToUse: Distributing images between build and runtime systems.

ShortDef: Describe and run several containers together from one YAML file.
Details: `docker compose up` starts the app, its database and anything else, with networks and volumes defined in `compose.yaml`. Ideal for local development and small deployments.
WhenToUse: A single host running a few related services.

ShortDef: Storage that outlives a container, so data survives restarts and upgrades.
Details: Container file systems are disposable. Databases and uploads belong on volumes (or managed services), and volumes need backups.
WhenToUse: Any container that holds data you care about.

ShortDef: A system that runs containers across many machines, restarts failures and scales on demand.
Details: You declare the desired state (this image, three copies, this config) and controllers make it true. Powerful, but heavy: many teams are better served by a simpler platform until they outgrow it.
WhenToUse: Running many services with high availability across a cluster.

ShortDef: Kubernetes' smallest deployable unit: one or more containers that share network and storage.
Details: You rarely create pods directly: a Deployment keeps the desired number running and rolls out updates, and a Service gives them a stable address.
WhenToUse: Understanding how Kubernetes runs and exposes your app.

ShortDef: The package manager for Kubernetes: install an app, with configurable values, in one command.
Details: A chart is a templated bundle of manifests. `helm install` and `helm upgrade` track releases so you can roll back.
WhenToUse: Installing third-party software or templating your own deployments.

ShortDef: Define servers, networks and cloud services in files, reviewed and versioned like software.
Details: Tools like Terraform and OpenTofu compare your files to reality and apply the difference. Everything is reproducible, reviewable and recoverable.
WhenToUse: Any infrastructure you expect to rebuild, copy or audit.

ShortDef: Automatically build and test every change (CI), then release it safely (CD).
Details: A pipeline runs on each commit: build, test, scan, package, deploy. Small frequent releases are safer than big rare ones.
WhenToUse: Any project with more than one contributor or more than one environment.

ShortDef: Git is the source of truth for what should run; an agent keeps the live system matching it.
Details: To change production you merge a pull request. Tools such as Argo CD and Flux watch the repository and reconcile the cluster, and drift is corrected automatically.
WhenToUse: Teams that want audited, reversible deployments.

ShortDef: Understanding what a system is doing from its logs, metrics and traces.
Details: Logs say what happened, metrics show trends (rate, errors, latency), traces follow one request across services. OpenTelemetry standardises collecting all three.
WhenToUse: Debugging production and knowing a problem exists before users tell you.

ShortDef: An open-source system that collects numeric metrics over time; Grafana draws them as dashboards.
Details: Prometheus scrapes endpoints on a schedule and stores time series; PromQL queries them and alert rules fire on thresholds.
WhenToUse: Metrics and alerting for services, containers and clusters.

ShortDef: A target for how reliable a service should be, measured so you know when to slow down and fix things.
Details: An SLI is the measurement (say, share of requests under 300 ms), the SLO is the goal (99.9%), and the error budget is how much failure you may spend. An SLA is the contract with customers.
WhenToUse: Deciding how much reliability work is enough.

ShortDef: A server in front of your apps that handles HTTPS, routing, caching and compression.
Details: Terminates TLS, forwards requests to the right backend and can add rate limits and headers. Forward the client's address with `X-Forwarded-*` headers and make the app trust them.
WhenToUse: Exposing one or many internal services to the internet.

ShortDef: The encryption behind HTTPS; certificates prove which site you are talking to.
Details: Let's Encrypt issues free certificates automatically. Renewal must be automated and monitored: expired certificates cause outages.

ShortDef: Release by running the new version beside the old one and switching traffic when it is healthy.
Details: Blue-green flips all traffic at once and can flip back; canary sends a small share first; rolling updates replace instances gradually. All avoid downtime and allow fast rollback.
